data.translation: Der Vater sprach: Ainilḥayat! - Was ist, Vater? - Mädchen, was ist denn mit der Stute, Balaridschla, los? - Es ist nichts, Vater. Ich bin eben einmal bei ihr aufgetaucht, und als sie mich sah, hat sie gewiehert. - Gut, meine Tochter.

rationale: Thin visiting cell: first-person feminine with b-pronominal mare target; retains the appearance/visit overlap.

summary: The current parsed input already distinguishes two visiting examples in Preterit Intransitive and nine sense-2 Infectum examples. Reader claims that all are tagged 1 concern an older compact display and do not justify structural edits here.

Appearance has the appearing person as subject (57/19; JTM 3.1/4; MAC Joseph/21); the visual construction has the observer as subject and village as ʕal target. The same preposition alone cannot settle the sense.

Intentional visiting overlaps appearing at a location. The Midyat request to look in on the wife (JTM 5.1/5) and visiting sisters at 95/153 show why a strict Kfarze-only gloss is inadequate; precise dialect geography remains open.
Authorized lookup of blq 2 shows stem II eye-opening, not the present stem-I observer construction; no homonym merger is made.
JTM 5.5/4 has a full Turoyo verse but no aligned translation. The reader's recovery claim from an adjacent verse cannot be verified from this record, so no example is quoted.

Collate inherited I naqqa ʕawwǝl d kobǝlqat aʕla with MAC NE Interview 2/223 I+naqabe dʕawwə́l kobəlqat aʕla: is 'first time' a misreading of 'mountain pass'? No text correction is made without collation.
Supply the aligned edition translation for JTM 5.5/4 before using it as an example.
Does the visiting sense extend throughout Midyat varieties, and where is the boundary between visiting and merely appearing at a place?
Is baliqina after aṯina at 95/153 coordinated Preterit Intransitive or a purpose-like use? The inherited form classification is retained provisionally.
Visit targets include a person/group with ʕal and a mare with b-, alongside inherited vineyard, family and sick-person targets.
